chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from Abu Ayyub al-Madani, the freedman of the Banu Hashim, from Dawud ibn Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Ja'fari, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no servant upon whom the bounties of Allah have become manifest, except that the provision/cost of the people upon him intensifies. So whoever does not attend to the needs of the people, he has exposed the bounty to perishing.' He said: 'I said: May I be your ransom, and who has the ability to attend to the needs of this creation?' He said: 'Rather, the people in this regard, by Allah, are the believers.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of failing to meet the needs of people when blessed with abundance?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of *Zawāl al-Ni‘mah* (vanishing of blessings), linking material prosperity directly to social accountability. He clarifies that the primary agents responsible for sustaining the community's welfare are the *al-Mu’minūn* (the believers), thereby elevating their role from passive recipients of grace to active stewards of divine favor.
